findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body: When callers invoke the returned cleanup function while the socket remains alive, the registered `"message"` handler remains active. Subsequent messages still reach disposed handlers, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners and duplicate work.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
For any EventEmitter-compatible socket, calling the returned cleanup function no longer unregisters `handler`. Subsequent `"message"` events invoke stale handlers after disposal, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate listeners.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
After a caller invokes the cleanup function, subsequent `"message"` events still invoke the handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message-listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
On a long-lived or reused socket, calling the returned disposer no longer retires the handler. Any later attacker-controlled `"message"` still reaches callbacks associated with an ended session or subscription, allowing stale-authority processing; repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate handlers and amplify CPU/memory usage per message.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
When callers invoke the returned disposer while the socket remains alive, the `"message"` listener stays registered and strongly retains its handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners, memory usage, and duplicate message-processing work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
